short: Text+ultrasound input to DNN-TTS (M06) is standard: test MCD falls 0.015-0.229 dB on 8 speakers; BAP, voicing worsen on test, F0 correlation improves; no listening test.
position: The paper changes one component: the acoustic model of a Merlin DNN-TTS receives 128 PCA coefficients of the ultrasound tongue image next to the linguistic features (M06) [@csapo2021txtult]. The network is the usual frame-wise fully connected regression, and by the paper's own account EMA served earlier as input to articulatory TTS (Sec. 5), so M06 is standard and new only in its sensor. Test MCD falls for all 8 speakers, by 0.015 to 0.229 dB, about 2% on average (Table 1; inference), on roughly 10 test sentences each (inference), runs not reported. Excitation is mixed: test F0 correlation rises for 6 of 8 speakers (Table 4), BAP error rises for 6 of 8 by at most 0.014 (Table 2) and voicing error rises for all 8 (Table 5; inference). The paper reports no listening test, yet concludes the input "may increase the naturalness" (Sec. 5). The ultrasound comes from the very utterance being scored, and the authors state that needing both inputs makes the system unsuitable for direct TTS or a Silent Speech Interface (Sec. 5).
